name: Kinetic
best_for: essays where the words are the picture
look: Essays where the words are the picture: one huge word on a turn, the clip pinned to a chalkboard with the line written under it in chalk, chalk line drawings that draw themselves (a lightbulb, a brain, an arrow, a clock, a target), white line-drawn stills that sketch themselves on, phone cards stacking then scattering round a serif title, a real comment with its phrases highlighted, headlines scrolling by, sources typed with a cursor. Lowercase techno-mono captions at the bottom, the key word yellow.
tagline: The words are the picture: clusters, white pages, phone cards, comments.

devices.use: one or two words of the sentence, huge and centred, one after another (a question, a turn)
a clip or a quote pinned on the chalkboard with the line written under it in chalk (inner = the words as the source itself captioned them, source = who said it)

a chalk icon drawn on the board for the idea of the moment (icon: lightbulb | brain | arrow | question | clock | dollar | heart | eye | gear | target | chart | person | fire | star | check | cross | book | phone | key | cloud) with 1-3 words beside it
1-3 short posts/videos as phone cards stacking up, then the episode's serif title typed
one real comment or post, the key phrases highlighted one after another (marks = 1-3 exact phrases from text)
2-4 real headlines scrolling by (bold = words to bold)
two pixelated pictures popping in with a caption, for a joke about what cannot be shown (can also sit on a clip: overlay frontier)
2-4 real sources or figures listed with a typing cursor.
where it happens (the template's map colours)
a real photo of a person named, in a pool of light

rules: Every graphic shows a real fact the voice gives at that moment (a name, a date, a place, a figure, a quote) - times come from the word timing, never before the narrator says it.
Footage: every 3-th shot sits in the board frame (frame='board'); clips under 5 s, chained when a line is longer; no talking heads, influencers or logos (QC).

This is an essay: the first minute opens on a bigword (one or two words of the opening question), a doodle (a chalk icon drawn for the idea: a lightbulb for an idea, a brain for thinking, a clock for time, a target for a goal, with 1-3 words beside it), then a board (the clip or the quote that set the question off, with the line written under it), a comment for the first real post quoted, and text labels for names and figures, and a spotlight (the real photo) on EVERY person named — an author, a scientist, an investor — the moment their name is said.

After the hook: footage carries it, every third shot pinned to the chalkboard; a doodle every 30-40 seconds on the idea of the moment (icons: lightbulb, brain, arrow, question, clock, dollar, heart, eye, gear, target, chart, person, fire, star, check, cross, book, phone, key, cloud); a board for a quote or a clip; a comment for every real post quoted; a sources card when studies or figures are listed; a scroll when several headlines are named; a bigword on every turn of the argument; a mosaic for a joke about what cannot be shown. Something new every 8 to 12 seconds. A spotlight with the real photo on every person named, every time a new name comes up; real footage of the thing named is always welcome between the drawings.

KINETIC: the caption gathers word by word left and right of the frame; big single words, white pages with typed lines, phone cards, real comments and headlines. Paste links to the studies, articles or videos you quote into Extra instructions.

ai_images.scene_prompt:
You are the art director for a faceless YouTube video.

CHANNEL: [INSERT CHANNEL HERE]

Below is the full spoken SCRIPT. Design [INSERT COUNT HERE] distinct background
SCENES that carry this video visually.

RULES
- Each scene illustrates a MOMENT the narrator actually reaches. Read the script
  and follow its order; scene 1 belongs at the start, the last at the end.
- Atmospheric imagery, never text on screen. No words, letters or numbers.
- No faces looking at camera unless the channel is built on a person.
- One subject per scene, described concretely: what is in frame, the light, the
  distance. "A hand resting on a closed book, low window light" — not "wisdom".
- Vary the distance across the set: wide, middle, close. A pool of fifteen
  medium shots edits like a slideshow.

Return ONLY a JSON array of [INSERT COUNT HERE] objects:

  {"text": "<the line of narration this scene belongs to>",
   "prompt": "<a complete image-generation prompt>"}

SCRIPT:
[INSERT SCRIPT HERE]
ai_images.still_suffix: Drawn EXACTLY like the reference: white hand-drawn marker lines on a pure black background, a single confident but imperfect hand, wobbly line weight, small gaps and overshoots, no shading, one small scribble of yellow or orange at most, no text, plenty of empty black space around the drawing, 16:9. Only the subject described, nothing else.
